From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0000
Subject: Transient throttle event — brief customer advisory (Sparrow Labs)

Hi Ava — quick heads up from the platform side. We observed a transient request-throttling pattern impacting some hosted inference endpoints in us-west between 07:52–08:05 UTC this morning which led to elevated p95 response times (and a small number of 429s).

What we did immediately:
- Routed affected traffic to a warmed fallback pool to re-stabilize latency within 2–3 minutes.
- Applied a dynamic capacity bump to the region; no model rollbacks required.
- Posted a brief incident notice to our status page (link below).

What we know so far:
- Scope: Sparrow Labs saw intermittent timeouts/429 for ~7 minutes; requests that hit retries succeeded.
- Cause (initial): a transient mismatch between autoscale signaling and the token-bucket throttle on a single serving shard. Full RCA in progress.

Next steps from us:
- We are collecting server-side traces and KV cache metrics. I attached a short summary of the mitigation timeline and the initial trace extract.
- ETA for an internal postmortem draft: EOD PT today. Public postmortem/summary for customers by tomorrow noon PT.

Can you confirm whether you saw any application-side errors or missing data during that window? Any client traces you can share would help speed the RCA.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/rl-2026-11-12-transient-throttle
Attachment: transient-throttle-summary-20261112.pdf (summary/timeline)

Thanks and sorry for the disruption — I’ll follow up as we have the RCA.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Marissa / Ben / Laura — forwarding Sparrow’s traces and the timeline. Short ask: please confirm customer-facing messaging and whether we should offer invoice credit for the spike.

Summary of proposed customer comms:
- Immediate: short advisory (done; status page)
- Follow-up: targeted summary of impact and mitigations + planned fix to autoscale/throttle coupling
- Compensation: recommend discretionary credit for any spike that caused downstream requeues; propose 10% credit on the affected window as a placeholder until finance weighs in.

Technical notes (from infra):
- Potential root cause: race between autoscaler downscale signal and token-bucket refill on one shard, which briefly reduced capacity below expected baseline.
- Short-term fix: enforce minimum warm-pool size and add an interlock between scale decisions and throttle thresholds.
- Long-term: add an observability alert for throttle-to-autoscale mismatch and a canary test during scale events.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Transient throttle event — brief customer advisory (Sparrow Labs) — postmortem & closure

Hi Ava / team — thanks again for the traces, and thank you Aditya for driving. Quick update and next steps after today’s triage: 

1) Impact: confirmed isolated to a single serving shard in us-west; Sparrow experienced elevated p95 and ~120 429 responses that were successfully retried. No evidence of data corruption or exposure.

2) Root cause (short): autoscaler allowed a transient shrink when a single shard misreported available tokens; throttle logic interpreted the reduced tokens as capacity and began rejecting new requests.

3) Fixes shipped / next actions:
- Immediate config change to enforce warm-pool minimum for serving nodes (deployed 15:10 PT).
- Patch queued to gate downscale decisions behind token-bucket health check (deploy by 11/15 EOD).
- Added dashboard + alert for throttle/autoscale divergence (INF-1245).

4) Billing & credits: Ben — can you review Sparrow’s spike volume and confirm recommended credit? My recommendation: waive token overage for the incident window; Ben, please confirm.

5) Public follow-up: we’ll publish a short customer-facing postmortem tomorrow detailing timeline, root cause, and mitigations. I’ll share the draft link for Sparrow review prior to publishing.

Meeting: Postmortem review scheduled — Google Calendar invite sent (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=postmortem-rl-20261112).

Closing note: we’re treating this as high priority; engineering has flagged a related small class of scale races for immediate test coverage.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
